Partly. I checked your installed Vitest (5.0.3). Vitest only catches this for its own async assertions: `expect(...).resolves` / `.rejects`, `expect.poll`, and browser-mode `expect.element`. If one of those is never awaited, Vitest throws "Promise returned by `…` was not awaited" when the test finishes, and the test **fails** instead of passing (see `node_modules/vitest/dist/chunks/index.C4tKZ0yW.js:1906`).

So if your test passed, the async part probably wasn't one of those. A common case is an async helper of your own that does the assertion inside it, or `expect(somePromise)` without `.resolves`, which checks the Promise object rather than the value it resolves to. Vitest can't see those. Add `await` (e.g. `await expect(p).resolves.toBe(x)`) and turn on the `@typescript-eslint/no-floating-promises` lint rule to catch the rest.
